newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned at hardships of Iraqis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned at hardships of Iraqis.

text.p: The United States expressed concern on Tuesday over reports that thousands of Iraqis are at risk this winter due to lack of essential goods, but continued to insist that President Saddam Hussein was to blame.
"The United States is deeply concerned about the plight of the Iraqi civilians who are victims of Saddam Hussein," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

U.N. aid agencies said on Monday thousands of people were threatened by lack of food, medicine and clean water in Iraq, partly due to U.N. sanctions imposed on Baghdad since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The sanctions ban Iraqi oil exports.
At a news conference in New York, agency officials estimated that 4,500 children were dying monthly.

Burns told a news briefing that the United States, a strong supporter of sanctions, wanted to "look more closely" at the figures quoted by the U.N. children's organisation UNICEF, some of which he said came from the Iraqi government.

"But regardless of the figures, UNICEF believes and the (U.N.) World Food Programme believes that conditions are actually deteriorating, they are getting worse in Iraq and that is cause of concern for the United States," he said.

Burns' comments appeared partly intended to modify his cool reaction on Monday to the U.N. statements, when he said the United States had no way of evaluating "the degree of the crisis" in Iraq because it had no diplomats there.
But, returning to a frequent theme, Burns argued that the problem lay in the way Saddam spent Iraq's money.

The Iraqi leader, he said, had spent the majority of the money on trying to rebuild the Iraqi army, on building palaces for himself and his relatives, on running a presidential yacht and on maintaining off-shore family bank accounts.

"Now, he has a choice here. He can decide maybe we won't put the yacht out on the Euphrates this year. He can decide maybe we'll shut down the palace for the winter ... and use that money to buy food and medicine on the international market," Burns said. "He's not making those decisions."

Iraqi officials, he said, were "very cynically" taking the Western press and Western relief organisations through Iraqi hospitals and orphanages to show "these heart-wrenching, terrible pictures of kids who are malnourished".
"And they are, and our hearts go out to those kids. But let's put the responsibility here where it lies. It lies with Saddam Hussein, and we should not be fooled by it", he said.

Burns said he was not suggesting that U.N. officials were being fooled by Saddam, and were merely "doing their job". But he said they were not as free to speak out about Saddam's responsibility as the United States.
